requirement_plain: Resource Deployment is currently a name-only placeholder master-data table (migration 0011, same pattern Resource Cost and Teams started from). Give it a real schema with TWO enforced foreign-key relationships instead of one: employeeId (required, numeric) must reference an existing Resources row by Resources' business key employee_id (not resources.id), reusing the exact validateReferences() mechanism FEAT-5 built for resource_cost.employeeId; positionId (required, string) must reference an existing Positions row by Positions' business key code (not positions.id) — this field was originally slated to be an unvalidated placeholder (matching modules.practiceId) only because Positions did not exist yet, but Positions now exists (FEAT-9, merged) so positionId must be a real enforced FK, not a manually-typed field. employeeName and positionName are NOT stored columns — both are live, read-time lookups (employeeName from the matched Resources row's current name, positionName from the matched Positions row's current name) via the existing generic lookups mechanism. This is the first master-data table needing two FK checks and two lookups concurrently, but the underlying framework (validateReferences() with Promise.all, multi-entry lookups array) was already built generically enough during FEAT-5/8/9 to need no changes. Writes happen only via the MCP server's add_resource_deployment/update_resource_deployment tools (frontend dashboard stays read-only), which must take employeeId (number) and positionId (string) only — never the derived name fields.

design_brief.summary: FEAT-7 upgrades resource_deployment from a name-only placeholder (migration 0011) to a real table with TWO validated foreign-key relationships (employeeId -> resources.employee_id, positionId -> positions.code) and TWO corresponding live-lookup response fields (employeeName, positionName). Unlike FEAT-5/8/9, which each introduced exactly one FK + one lookup, this is the first table exercising the generic framework's multi-field capability end to end — concurrent validateReferences() checks via Promise.al, and a multi-entry lookups array — both already built and proven ahead of this need. No framework changes are anticipated; this is purely a descriptor-and-migration task layered on existing, working machinery.
in_scope: New migration (backend/migrations/0016_...) dropping the placeholder name column and adding employee_id (numeric, required, FK to resources.employee_id) and position_code (string, required, FK to positions.code) to resource_deployment, following the 0013 pattern (empty-table single-phase drop, fk_<table>_<ref_table> constraint + ix_<table>_<fk_column> index for each of the two new FK columns)
Applying that migration live via mcp__Supabase__apply_migration

Backend: two `references` descriptor entries on resource_deployment's field list (employeeId -> resources.employee_id, positionId -> positions.code), two `lookups` entries (resources.name -> employeeName, positions.name -> positionName), and a `sortColumn` override (e.g. employee_id) replacing the dropped name field as sort key

MCP server: mirrored field descriptor update in mcp-server/src/masterDataTables.js exposing only employeeId (number) and positionId (string) as writable, matching resource_cost/position labeling style
New test file backend/src/masterDataRouter.resourceDeployment.test.js on the shared harness, covering both FK fields and both lookups per REQ-8
out_of_scope: Any write UI/form on the frontend (dashboard stays read-only per the task)
Any change to the generic validateReferences()/lookups framework itself — this feature is explicitly scoped as descriptor-only, framework already proven
Changing Resources', Positions', or any other sibling table's own schema
The unvalidated-placeholder approach for positionId — explicitly superseded now that Positions exists; must not be built even as a fallback
open_questions_for_architecture: Confirm the FK column name should be position_code (not position_id) per the departmentCode/teamCode column-naming convention, even though the API/JSON key is positionId — codebase-explorer flagged this naming distinction but it is a naming decision, not a requirement, for the Solution Architect/System Engineer stages to confirm
Confirm sortColumn choice (employee_id vs. another column) once the System Engineer stage finalizes the column list
Soft-deleted-reference read-path behavior (inherited ambiguity from FEAT-5, applies to both new lookups here) remains a framework-level open item, not newly introduced by this feature

process_note: Per codebase-explorer's stage-0.5 findings, the generic FK/lookup framework in backend/src/masterDataSchema.js already supports everything this feature needs without modification, including concurrent multi-field validation and multi-entry lookups (built during FEAT-5's gate specifically ahead of a table needing exactly this). This analysis assigns no new framework requirements — all nine requirements above are descriptor-application and migration work, consistent with the explorer's PASS verdict that later stages can proceed directly to implementation.
